name: Broken Access Control
description: Users can act outside their intended permissions.
remediation: Deny by default, enforce server-side object authorization, and test tenant boundaries.

name: Cryptographic Failures
description: Sensitive data lacks appropriate modern cryptographic protection.
remediation: Use TLS, modern authenticated encryption, managed keys, and strong password hashing.

name: Injection
description: Untrusted data is interpreted as a command or query.
remediation: Use parameterized interfaces, context-aware encoding, and strict input validation.

name: Insecure Design
description: Required security controls are absent from the design.
remediation: Use threat modeling, secure design patterns, and abuse-case acceptance criteria.

name: Security Misconfiguration
description: Unnecessary features, defaults, or verbose errors expose attack surface.
remediation: Apply repeatable hardened configurations and remove unused capabilities.

name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
description: Dependencies contain known vulnerabilities or are unsupported.
remediation: Maintain an SBOM, continuously scan dependencies, and apply supported updates.

name: Identification and Authentication Failures
description: Authentication, session, or credential recovery controls can be bypassed.
remediation: Use MFA, secure session rotation, rate limits, and resistant password recovery.

name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
description: Untrusted updates, pipelines, or serialized data compromise integrity.
remediation: Verify signatures, protect CI dependencies, and use safe serialization.

name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
description: Attacks cannot be detected or investigated from security telemetry.
remediation: Centralize tamper-resistant security events, alerting, and tested response procedures.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery
description: The server fetches an attacker-selected resource.
remediation: Allowlist destinations, enforce network egress policy, and reject redirect-based bypasses.
